name: Lamborghini Urus
designer: Filippo Perini (2012 concept); Mitja Borkert (production version)

kerbWeight.sourceNote: Base Urus. Confirmed independently by NHTSA's Canadian Vehicle Specifications for the 2019 model year, which records the identical 2,200 kg curb weight.

displacement.sourceNote: The article states the engine as "4.0-litre", based on the Audi 4.0 TFSI V8; 3,996 cc is that engine family's well-documented displacement, not a figure stated directly in this article.

mass.sourceNote: Confirmed by NHTSA's Canadian Vehicle Specifications for the 2019 model year.

weightDistributionFront.sourceNote: Published as a 58/42 front/rear split for the 2019 model year. The split is nose-heavy for a Lamborghini, consistent with its front-engine layout, unlike every mid-engined car in the range.

trims.name: Urus SE
trims.transmission: 8-speed ZF 8HP automatic with integrated electric motor

engine.configuration: V8, twin-turbo, plug-in hybrid with permanent-magnet electric motor

displacement.sourceNote: Reworked version of the same Audi-derived 4.0-litre V8; the article does not give an exact cc figure for the SE's engine, so this carries the same estimate as the base Urus.

power.sourceNote: Published combined system output. The engine alone makes 462 kW and the electric motor alone 141 kW; those do not add to 596 kW because they peak at different points, so only the manufacturer's own combined figure is used.

torque.sourceNote: Published combined system torque. The engine alone makes 800 N-m and the motor alone 483 N-m; motor and engine torque cannot be meaningfully summed at the crankshaft, so only the manufacturer's own combined figure is used.

batteryCapacity.sourceNote: Total pack capacity; the article does not separately state a usable figure.

topSpeed.sourceNote: Lamborghini's own claim: the fastest production SUV in the world at launch.

mass.sourceNote: The article states only that the SE is "roughly 300 kg" heavier than the Urus S due to its 25.9 kWh battery pack, and the Urus S's own kerb weight is not independently stated in this article, only the original Urus's 2,200 kg. Adding 300 kg to a different trim's weight would be exactly the kind of invented arithmetic this site avoids, so the field is left as a placeholder instead.

hero.caption: The Urus SE, Lamborghini's plug-in hybrid update of its front-engined SUV and, at launch, the fastest production SUV in the world.

gallery.caption: The Urus Performante, a lighter and more powerful variant introduced in 2022.

gallery.caption: The original 2019 Urus, powered by a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 shared in modified form with Audi.
